full_judgment:
A.K.M Sadeque, J.: This Second Appeal by the Plaintiffs arises out of a suit for partition being Title Suit No. 200 of 1970 of the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet. Plaintiffs brought the suit alleging that Defendant No. 1 Abdus Sattar (since deceased) was the owner of the partiable land comprising C.S. Plots No. 950 and 951, described in the schedule to the plaint. He sold 9 annas 15 gds share of the suit land to Abdul Aziz by a kabala, dated 6.12.1926. While in possessions Hazi Abdul Aziz died survived by his father Nassarullah as his sole heir. Nassarullah possessed of the land died survived by his daughter and only heir Najibunnessa. While in possession she sold the land by Kabala dated 18.8.44 to Moula Ali, Maula Ali possessed the land on the basis of his purchase and sold it together with other lands to the Plaintiffs by three different kabalas dated 2nd Chaitra, 1374 B.S. The Plaintiffs got their names mutated in the records of right. The suit land was not partitioned by metes and bounds and there were frequent disputes with the Defendants No. 1-3, who were their co-sharers, over possession. So, the Plaintiffs requested the Defendants No. 1-3 in Bhadra 1374 B.S. for partition, but to no effect. This gave rise to the cause of action. It was also alleged by the Plaintiffs that at the time of execution and registration of the kabalas, they were not in possession of the khatian. So, in the kabala, only C.S. Dag No. 950 was written, but the boundary, as given in the schedule to the plaint, would a attract C.S. dag no. 951. 

 2. The suit was contested by the Defendants Nos. 1-3 who filed a joint Written Statement. These Defendants contended that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and the suit was bad defect of parties. Their substantive contention was that Defendant No. 1 (since deceased) sold 9 annas 15 gds share of the suit land to Hazi Azizullah by kabala dated 6.12.1926 and delivered possession of the same in his favour. Thereafter, the Defendant No. 1 took rayati settlement of the self-same land from Kazi Azizullah on 10th Baishakh, 1339 B.S. corresponding to 22.5.1932. Since then, the Defendant No. 1 had possessed the suit land asserting his own title beyond the statutory period of 12 years to perfect his title, by constructing huts, residing there, and plucking fruits from the trees of the suit land. After coming into force of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the Defendant No. 1 had possessed the suit land under the Government as rayati and, accordingly, it was recorded in the khatian in his own name. Hazi Moula Ali never possessed the suit land as his house was about 5 miles away from it. The contesting Defendants denied all the material allegations made in the plaint and prayed for dismissal of the suit. The learned Subordinate Judge raised the following issues. 

 3. The Subordinate Judge answered the issue 1 in the affirmative and 2 in the negative, with observation that no contest was made before him over these issues. The learned Subordinate Judge found the issues 3 and 4 in affirmative and decreed the suit in full. The learned Subordinate Judge proceeded on the reasoning’s that the sale by the Defendant No. 1 in favour of Hazi Azizullah and succession of Hazi Azizullah by his father Nasarullah and Nasarullah by his daughter Najibunnessa, sale by Najibunnessa to Syed Maula Ali by Ext 2C dated 18.8.44 and final sale by Syed Maula Ali in favour of the Plaintiff by kabala Ext. 2-2(b) dated 2nd Chaitra 1374 B.S. corresponding to 6.3.68 were undisputed facts. He also noticed that 9 annas 15 gds share of the suit land had been recorded in the name of Maula Ali and the Plaintiffs (on the basis of mutation) vide khatian Exts. 1 and 1(a). The learned Subordinate Judge considered the oral evidence on record and found possession of Syed Maula Ali and, subsequently, of the Plaintiff in the suit land. He particularly relied upon the evidence of P.Ws 2 and 3 who were the sons of Syed Maula Ali. Coming to the defence case, the learned Subordinate Judge found that the Defendants could not produce, except certified copy of the Kobyliyat Ext. A, any documents of settlement and any rent receipts to show that the Defendants ever paid any rents and that the kobulyat Ext. A or the subsequent un-registered koblyats were acted upon. The learned Subordinate Judge noticed and laid great stress upon the fact that the kabala Ext 2(c) executed by Najimunnessa in favour of Syed Maula All was written by Abdus Sattar, Defendant No. 1 who was no other than the father-in-law of Syed Maula Ali. In this Kabala Ext. 2C, he pointed out, there was no indication that 9 annas 15 gds share of the superior interest was sold; on the contrary, the recital of the kabala shows that khash land and possessory interest were sold by the said kabala. The learned Subordinate Judge discussed the defence witnesses and disbelieved them. 

 9. Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the Respondents, on the other hand, has squarely supported the judgment of the learned Additional District Judge and stated that the inspection report and other evidence on record have conclusively established the possession of the Defendants in plot No. 951 and the Plaintiffs also did not purchase any share of Plot No. 954 but they purchased, if at all, share of Plot No. 950. Therefore, the learned Additional District Judge did not commit any illegality in reversing the judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge and dismissing the suit. Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury further submitted that the suit land as described in the khatian and the plaint as a homestead and the kobulyat Ext. A would show that the Defendant No. 1 (deceased) had taken settlement for residence and enjoyment of usufructs of the suit land. So the suit land of dag No. 951 was a non-agricultural land and the Defendant No. 1 was a non-agricultural tenant, within the meaning of Section 7, Sub-Section 4 and 5 of the Non-agricultural Tenancy Act. Therefore, the tenancy was protected under Section 7, Sub section 4 and 5(1) of the said Act. Since, he submitted, much more than 12 years had elapsed from the date of Ext A and according to the pleader commissioner's report and also the Court of Additional District Judge who is the final Court of fact, the Defendants have been in possession in plot No. 951, the Plaintiffs have no right to get Partition in respect of these plots and evict the Defendant in course of such partition.
